description: Operation-boundary validation under the applicable dialect with format as annotation and ECMA-262 u-mode patterns, in the OBI document's resolution context, per value, with no verdict where the result depends on a missing reference or capability, the result is undefined, or no contract is stated.

scenarios.description: A value satisfying a complete governing schema validates successfully.
An available graph that rejects the instance reports instance mismatch.
Format is annotation-only at the operation boundary by default; this scenario runs without the format-assertion option JSON Schema lets a tool offer.
A multi-value interaction validates each value independently rather than as one aggregate.
An absolute reference satisfied by an embedded schema identifier is locally available.
Same-document references resolve from the OBI document root when an operation schema is evaluated.
An absent input states no contract: no verdict, success included.
An absent output states no contract: no verdict, success included.
input: true is a stated contract every value satisfies.
input: false is a stated contract no value satisfies.
A required reference the tool does not have gives no verdict.
A mismatch that depends on a missing reference gives no verdict; a success that does not depend on it may be reported.
A cycle that recurses without consuming the instance is undefined: no verdict.
Within an $id resource, a pointer that reaches no schema is undefined: no verdict.
Within an $id resource, a plain name declared twice is undefined: no verdict.
An inline modifier group is not an ECMA-262 (11th edition) pattern: undefined, no verdict.
An identity escape the u flag forbids is not a valid pattern: undefined, no verdict.
An invalid patternProperties name makes the result undefined wherever it applies: no verdict.
ECMA-262 \s matches Unicode white space and line terminators.
ECMA-262 \d matches ASCII digits only.
With the u flag, . matches one code point outside the Basic Multilingual Plane.
$ matches only at the end of input, not before a trailing newline.
A pattern is not anchored: it matches anywhere in the string.
patternProperties names are ECMA-262 patterns with Unicode semantics.
A Unicode property escape matches under the u flag; a tool declaring the feature unsupported must give no verdict, even a correct one.
OpenAPI 3.0's nullable is an unknown keyword under 2020-12 (section 5.2).
The legacy dependencies keyword is not a 2020-12 assertion: the 2020-12 meta-schema keeps it only to validate its form.
Content keywords are annotations under 2020-12 (JSON Schema Validation, content vocabulary).
A plain name declared in the document resource resolves.
A percent-encoded plain name is decoded before lookup.
A percent-encoded JSON Pointer is decoded before evaluation.
A relative reference inside an $id resource resolves against its base.
A $dynamicRef inside an $id resource resolves through the dynamic scope to the document resource's $dynamicAnchor (section 7.5).
An array schema is applied to each value, never to the values as one array.
An external reference resolves to a resource the tool accepts; a tool that declines supplied resources must give no verdict.
format: regex is an annotation, separate from the pattern keyword.
An example outside the schema does not widen the contract (formerly T11-S-03).
Examples do not narrow the contract to themselves (formerly T11-S-04).
An example does not override an enum (formerly T11-S-05).
A result that does not depend on an invalid pattern may be reported: anyOf succeeds or fails on the first branch's type alone.
A dormant property schema with an invalid pattern does not decide a value that lacks the property.
Numbers are compared at their exact value: 2^53 + 1 is not 2^53.
multipleOf is decided on exact decimal values.
An external schema declaring draft-07 is evaluated under draft-07, where dependencies asserts; a tool without that dialect or the resource gives no verdict.
An example checked against a schema with a missing reference gets no verdict (section 5.1: a checker evaluates the value as any other).
An example checked against an undefined schema (a non-productive cycle) gets no verdict.
A percent-encoded pointer is decoded before lookup even when the literal spelling also names a property: my%20type means 'my type'.

A schema resource without $schema takes its enclosing resource's dialect (section 5.2, JSON Schema Core section 9.3.2): the inner resource is draft-07, where dependencies asserts; a tool without that dialect gives no verdict.
A string that is not a well-formed URI-reference is not a reference of any form, and a value whose evaluation depends on it has an undefined result (section 7.1): no verdict through a raw space.
A modifier group (?i:...) is not a pattern under the pinned ECMA-262 11th edition (section 13.1): undefined, no verdict, even where a newer engine accepts it.
Within an $id resource, a pointer that reaches a map rather than a schema is undefined (section 7.4): no verdict.
The resolution context is the OBI document's own resources: an $id that claims the 2020-12 meta-schema's URI names the document's schema, not the meta-schema.
A malformed reference has an undefined result only for an evaluation that depends on it (section 7.1): type fails 5 whatever #%zz would yield, so a mismatch is permitted, and so is declining.
anyOf with true holds for any value whatever a malformed sibling reference would yield (section 7.1): valid is permitted, and so is declining.
Inside an $id resource, a $ref that is not a URI-reference (a raw space) has no defined target (JSON Schema Core section 8.2.3.1): no verdict for a value that needs it.
A $schema in the document resource declares no dialect (section 5.2), so a foreign one there leaves the schema read as 2020-12: a tool that continues reports the mismatch or declines.
A $schema in the document resource declares no dialect (section 5.2), even one that is not a string: a tool that continues reports the 2020-12 verdict or declines.
\p{EBase} names no property in the pinned ECMA-262 11th edition (section 13.1; ECMA-262 section 21.2.1.1, Table 56): the pattern is invalid, so no verdict.
Script=Kawi is not a script value in the pinned ECMA-262 11th edition (section 13.1; ECMA-262 Table 58): the pattern is invalid, so no verdict.
Two schemas declaring one $id leave a reference to it with no defined target (JSON Schema Core section 9.1.2): no verdict.

With the document resource outermost in the dynamic scope (section 7.2), a $dynamicRef the document resource captures through a $dynamicAnchor it declares twice has no defined target (JSON Schema Core sections 8.2.3.2, 8.2.2): no verdict.
